newsitem.title: USA: USWC Lt. crudes rise with WTI, buyers watch heavy.
newsitem.headline: USWC Lt. crudes rise with WTI, buyers watch heavy.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices were higher in line with West Texas Intermediate (WTI), traders said Wednesday, souring refiners who were already shifting their buying interest to heavy grades.
"Everyone's trying to figure out what's going on with California heavies," a trader said.
Traders said Tosco turned away delivery of February heavies Monday following a fire at its Calif. plant.
With heavy crude prices expected to drop below their current $17.40 range, refiners were looking at ways to run heavies instead of light grades.
Meanwhile, short covering of heating oil lifted WTI crudes 45 cents a barrel higher to $24.30/24.40 in eastern U.S. markets.
Outright ANS prices rose the same amount, as a lack of buying interest kept the differential at $1.45 under March WTI. ANS ranged $22.80/24 a barrel.
"You could get a huge difference between heavy and light crudes," a trader said.
BP America, a key producer, was asking for $1.25 below March NYMEX, with not buyers stepped forward in early trade.

California oil companies offered heavy oil at an average price of $17.40, or about $1.50 less than three weeks ago. Traders reported cargoes sold at 50 to 25 cents under those averages and expected further declines.
Outright prices for Kern River, a representative heavy grade, were offered at $17.55 and bid about $17.30.
